newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares edge up in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: China B shares edge up in sluggish trade.

text.p: China's B share indices edged up in sluggish trade on Thursday, with investors moving to the sidelines in light of recent bearish trends and warnings from Beijing over trading irregularities, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index inched up 0.145 points, or 0.17 percent, to 83.225 while the Shenzhen market crept up 0.01 of a point to end at 146.63.

Volume on both markets was sluggish, with Shanghai turnover coming in at a thin $7.892 million, compared with Wednesday's $9.246 million and that in Shenzhen at HK$42 million, up from Wednesday's HK$40 million.
Recent crackdown measures by Beijing have dampened sentiment and an official warning on Wednesday against illegal trading and disclosure practices was making many investors lie low, brokers said.
"Sentiment in both the A and B share markets has turned weak after the recent poor performance and there are no signs of immediate recovery," said Cheng Li, an analyst at China Guotai Securities.

Shanghai B shares were lifted by heavily traded Pudong counters and newcomer Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle Co 900946.SS, which crept up $0.004 to $0.532 on the day's heaviest volume of 3.26 million shares, brokers said.
Pudong-based Shanghai Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development Co Ltd and Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development also ended slightly up on solid turnover.

Shenzhen's A index slipped 6.69 points, or 1.56 percent, to 421.60 due partly to profit-taking in giant newcomer First Auto Works Car Co Ltd, and Shanghai's A market dipped 0.17 percent, or 2.149 points, to 1,285.014.
Turnover in the Shenzhen market shrank to 5.1 billion yuan from seven billion yuan in the previous session while Shanghai's volume remained close to Wednesday's at about 3.9 billion yuan.

Investors were also cautious on concerns over A share leader Shenzhen Development Bank, which Beijing last week suspended for five days after sacking its president for illegal stock trading, brokers said.
"Most investors are unmoved because of possible new measures to curb the speculative mood especially in the A share market," one broker said.
Beijing on Wednesday also warned listed firms not to falsify financial statements to cover up losses or speculate in their own shares.
"If there is a too sharp rise, it will attract government attention and result in new crackdown measures," another broker said.
The markets would likely move in a narrow range in the next two weeks in the run-up to the July 1 return of the British colony of Hong Kong to Chinese rule, one trader said.
Brokers in Shenzhen said they expected the B share market to maintain sluggish trading in the 140-150 point range for some time, but added relatively cheap prices would prevent further heavy selling.
In the Shanghai B index, hotel group Shanghai Jinjiang Tower Co was the star on speculative buying ahead of the close, jumping $0.028, or 8.18 percent, to $0.370.
Shanghai Rubber Belt Co Ltd was the day's sharpest loser, plunging $0.20 to finish 10 percent limit down at $0.180.
In Shenzhen's B share market, automobile parts maker Wuxi Weifu was the sharpest gainer, rising HK$0.30, or 6.19 percent, to HK$5.15 on volume of 285,000 shares. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
